recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is and do not reintroduce the core ConceptMap profile source unless FHIR-37959 or the CRMI ownership decision is revisited. Any remaining work about profile hosting or core-to-CRMI references should be handled under FHIR-37959 or CRMI/THO publication work.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive Vocab issue requesting Shareable and Publishable ConceptMap profiles based on the Shareable and Publishable patterns for R5.
initial_application: PR #2068, merged as 0d4401be with implementation commit 93fadfaa, added source/conceptmap/structuredefinition-profile-shareableconceptmap.xml and source/conceptmap/structuredefinition-profile-publishableconceptmap.xml and registered them in source/conceptmap/implementationguide-ConceptMap-core.xml. The R5 history bundle still includes both StructureDefinition/shareableconceptmap and StructureDefinition/publishableconceptmap entries.
additional_context: FHIR-37959 later reached Applied/Persuasive for R6 and decided to remove Shareable/Publishable/Computable/Executable profiles from core FHIR and maintain them in CRMI. May 2025 Vocab/CDS/CQI minutes confirm the 16-0-0 direction that these profiles should remain in CRMI because they evolve quickly and need that context. Commit 3958dd1e removed the ConceptMap profile registrations and related introduction pages from core.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current absence of Shareable/Publishable ConceptMap profile source is a later intentional R6 migration, not an unapplied FHIR-37845 defect.

related_jiras.note: Applied R6 decision to remove these profile families from core and maintain them in CRMI, superseding the current-build effect of FHIR-37845.
